payload.content:
# Field Notes: Seattle Tech Office, March 2025

## Location
Large tech company, downtown Seattle. Open plan office, 200+ employees.

## Initial Observations

Arrived 8:45am. Coffee machine area usually busy - this morning felt different. Only 3 people waiting instead of usual 10-15. Overheard Sarah (PM) mention to James that their usual supplier is "having issues with shipments."

## Mid-Morning (10:30am)

Stood near coffee station for 20 minutes. Noticed people lingering longer than usual. Small talk about weekend plans, projects. Tom from engineering: "Anyone else notice the coffee tastes... different? Like they changed brands?"

Maria (HR): "They probably had to switch suppliers. I heard there are shortages in Brazil or something."

## Lunch Period Observations

Cafeteria at 12:15pm. Counted 8 people bringing their own thermoses - unusual. Asked casual question to Rachel (designer) about it.

Rachel: "Oh yeah, I started bringing coffee from home. The office stuff has been inconsistent lately. Plus I like my fancy beans." *laughs* "First world problems, right?"

## Afternoon Energy Levels

2-3pm typically slowest period. Today seemed normal. No unusual napping or fatigue. Standard 2:30pm "coffee run" happened - group of 5 went to cafe across street.

## Coffee Machine Interactions

3:45pm observation: Noticed the conversation *quality* at machine. Not just weather talk. Mike and Jennifer having actual discussion about project challenges. Lasted maybe 8 minutes. Mike: "We never actually talk anymore, just Slack. This is nice."

## End of Day

5pm. People leaving at normal pace. Energy seems fine. Productivity appeared normal from external observation - lots of focused work, meetings running on time.

## Researcher Reflections

Baseline observation. Coffee availability still good, just slight anxiety about supply. Social patterns at coffee machine seem *enhanced* by slight scarcity - people savoring the moment more? Need more data.

No signs of crisis. This feels like typical corporate life with minor supply chain hiccup. Will follow up in 6 weeks.
